title: bug: moe-account-switch never rotates an interactive seat at a hard usage limit when another plugin swallows classic.StopFailure
description:
Observed 2026-10-24: architect-26ba32c3 is an interactive TUI on acct-2 (wrapper pid 201785, started 13:57Z) holding R01. At 15:49:09Z it hit "You've hit your session limit · resets 9:30pm". It should have run /exit so the wrapper could relaunch it on the next account. Instead it sat idle until claude's own auto-continue at the reset, 18:30Z, about 2h41m later.

The transcript (acct-2 projects/-mnt-d-projexts-moes/8edd9b5c-….jsonl) records the engine's notice: `moe-account-switch: its classic.StopFailure hook was skipped. "cc-plugin-sec-default" runs first and sent the event on past it.`

scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/hooks/register.ts:109-118 is the mod's only hard-limit trigger. So any plugin ordered ahead of it that does not pass StopFailure on disables limit rotation for every interactive seat (architect and governor TUIs). Headless seats are unaffected, because their wrapper detects the failed run.

Suggested direction (the architect decides): do not depend solely on StopFailure. Also check `$.session.usage()` rateLimits ≥100% where the mod already runs for the main loop (turn.complete), and leave() from there. Keep the existing StopFailure path. Confirm the engine's hook ordering, and whether turn.complete fires on a rate-limit stop, with the plugin-authoring skill.
definitionOfDone: A main-loop turn that ends at a hard usage limit (any rate-limit window at 100% or more) schedules the seat's /exit even when classic.StopFailure never reaches the mod (e.g. an earlier plugin does not pass it on).

No exit is scheduled for a subagent turn, for a session without MOE_WORKER_ID and MOE_ACCOUNT_ID, or for a turn that ends with every window below 100%; the existing StopFailure and accountSwitch paths keep working.
hooks/register.test.ts covers the skipped-StopFailure case and the three no-exit cases, and fresh `claude plugin test scripts/mods/moe-account-switch` passes with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Fail open, as the mod does today: an error in the new check must leave the turn and the session as they were.

Reproduce the real skip using test(name, {plugins:[{name:'swallow-stop-failure', tier:'prepend', register(on){on('classic.StopFailure', () => ({}))}}]}, body). With SEAT, a main turn.start, and a usage window at 100, fire classic.StopFailure then turn.complete({...TURN,turnId:'t1',reason:'error'}). Assert the bottom StopFailure stub was NOT reached, no exit was scheduled by the swallowed event, completion returns {text:'ok'} unchanged, and clock.advance(EXIT_DELAY_MS-1) yields commands=[], then advance(1) yields ['exit'] with one toast. Also cover turn.complete alone with NO StopFailure dispatch; mixed windows [99.9,100] and >100 on a non-five_hour window; all-below [0,99.9] and empty rateLimits. At 100%, assert no toast/exit/usage read for a subagent completion and for each environment missing worker, missing account, or both; after the subagent, an eligible main completion still exits. Add usage/env failure cases asserting the original completion result is preserved, downstream completion executes once, no pending work refusal/exit is introduced, and a later successful check still works. Verify pre-existing pending accountSwitch still exits even when the usage stub would throw (it must not be read). Cover StopFailure followed by completion, reverse order, and repeated/concurrent completion with exactly one timer/toast/exit; retain all existing accountSwitch/StopFailure tests. Use the mock clock, not real timers. The skipped-hook test must fail against the old implementation; record red proof during the TDD cycle, with the single full regression gate reserved for step 4.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum shared hard-limit check with fail-open error handling. Add a small internal async helper taking ($, session): `if (session.pending || !(await isSeat($))) return; const { rateLimits } = await $.session.usage(); if (rateLimits.some(window => window.percentUsed >= 100)) session.pending ??= <the existing hard-limit ACCOUNT-SWITCH instruction>;`. Reuse the existing message verbatim; ??= after the await preserves a concurrently delivered daemon instruction. In turn.complete retain `const done = await next(e)`; for `e.agentId === undefined`, await this helper then call leave($, session), and return the original done. Do not gate on reason==='error': the contract is any main completion with a spent window. Keep the existing `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))`, whose next is replay-safe, so env/usage failures occur before state mutation and preserve the completed turn. Have classic.StopFailure reuse the helper after its existing error==='rate_limit', no agent_id and no-pending guards; retain leave there and its catch. Do not call command.run inside an awaited hook, change the 10-second delay, change isSeat, add polling, or alter the held-tool/accountSwitch policy. Preserve leave's exiting guard so both event paths and concurrent completions schedule only one exit. Add a short why-comment that classic.StopFailure may be skipped by an earlier mod.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented shared checkHardLimit using existing isSeat/pending/leave; main completion independently checks any window >=100, StopFailure reuses it, daemon instruction preserved via ??= after await.
